description: Known failure signatures for 2010 MacBook Pro SATA cable and related boot issues

patterns.name: SATA Cable Failure — Classic
patterns.description: The SATA ribbon cable connecting the HDD to the logic board has failed or degraded. The Mac cannot detect the internal drive at boot time.
patterns.root_cause: Worn or cracked 821-0814-A / 821-1226-A SATA ribbon cable causing intermittent or total loss of drive connectivity.
repair_steps: Boot into Internet Recovery (Cmd+Opt+R) to confirm drive is not detected in Disk Utility.
Connect an external USB drive with macOS — if it boots, the internal SATA cable is suspect.
Replace the SATA ribbon cable (821-0814-A for 13-inch, 821-1226-A for 15-inch).
Reseat the HDD connector on both the logic board and the drive before ordering parts.
After cable replacement, reinstall macOS via Recovery Mode.

patterns.name: Kernel Panic — Drive I/O Error
patterns.description: Repeated kernel panics caused by AHCI port errors — the drive is losing connectivity mid-session rather than at cold boot.
patterns.root_cause: Intermittent SATA cable failure causing I/O errors that trigger kernel panics. Correlates with heat (cable near GPU exhaust) or physical flex.
repair_steps: Run Apple Diagnostics (D at boot) — look for HDD or storage errors.
In Terminal: 'sudo fsck -fy /dev/disk0s2' to check filesystem integrity.
Check /var/log/system.log for AppleAHCIPort errors.
Replace SATA cable. If panics persist after cable replacement, test HDD with SMART tools.
Consider replacing HDD with an SSD — eliminates mechanical failure and reduces cable stress.

patterns.name: Prohibitory Symbol — OS Corruption
patterns.description: macOS detects the drive but cannot load a valid system from it. Caused by OS corruption, a missing System folder, or a SATA cable causing partial read errors.
patterns.root_cause: Incomplete macOS installation, filesystem corruption, or cable-induced read errors during a prior write operation.
repair_steps: Boot into Recovery Mode (Cmd+R) — if successful, the cable is likely functional.
Run First Aid in Disk Utility on the startup disk.
If disk appears healthy, reinstall macOS from Recovery.
If Disk Utility shows the disk as unmountable or with errors, suspect cable AND drive.
Replace SATA cable, then attempt recovery again.
parts_needed: 821-0814-A or 821-1226-A SATA cable (if drive errors persist)

patterns.name: Spinning Globe / Slow Boot — EFI Fallback
patterns.description: The Mac is falling back to Internet Recovery or NetBoot, indicating the local drive was not detected at firmware level.
patterns.root_cause: SATA cable not presenting the drive to EFI firmware; same root cause as P001 but the firmware falls back to network boot instead of showing a question mark.
repair_steps: Allow Internet Recovery to load — then open Disk Utility to confirm drive visibility.
If drive is not shown in Disk Utility, SATA cable replacement is required.
If drive is shown but blank, reinstall macOS.
After cable replacement, reset NVRAM (Cmd+Opt+P+R) to clear boot device preference.

patterns.name: Clicking / Grinding HDD
patterns.description: Mechanical hard drive failure — audible clicking or grinding indicates read head failure (click of death).
patterns.root_cause: Physical HDD failure independent of, but worsened by, a degraded SATA cable causing repeated reconnection attempts.
repair_steps: STOP — do not power cycle the drive. Continued spinning worsens head damage.
Data recovery must be prioritised: seek a professional data recovery service.
Replace the HDD with an SSD to eliminate mechanical failure risk entirely.
Replace the SATA cable simultaneously — cable degradation accelerates HDD wear.
Do not attempt to boot from the failing drive again.
